name: Reuse of treated wastewater for irrigation (ONAS plants, national reuse strategy, perimeters supplied with treated water)
owner: ONAS (treatment and tertiary upgrades); MARHP and its regional offices (CRDA) and water user groups (GDA) for distribution and irrigated perimeters; Ministries of Environment and Health for authorisation

claims.claim: Tunisia aims for a treated-wastewater use rate of 80% by 2050 (ministry sector report) and earlier set a goal of reusing 50% or more of treated water (2016-2020 plan, as reported by JICA).
Low reuse is mainly a treatment-quality problem; upgrading plants to tertiary treatment will make the water usable and bring about 3,357 ha under irrigation from 18 to 19 plants (PAQEE-RCC).
The first phase (PAQEE, 2012) rehabilitated about thirty plants with potential to irrigate 12,500 ha and 4,000 farmers, with positive farmer feedback.
Farmers accept treated water (80% hypothetical acceptance) and it is cheap (TND 0.02/m3 since 1997).
Solar PV at tertiary plants (6,000 kWc, 1,887 tCO2eq/year avoided) offsets the energy cost of added treatment.

limits: Treated water is a fixed volume tied to sewage collected, about 293 million m3 a year (SRC-TG-530, SRC-TG-650). Even 100% use would equal about 26% of the 1,139 Mm3 deficit projected for 2050 (SRC-TG-504 via FND-TG-501), before any growth in effluent.
Where plants are far from farmland (Greater Tunis, coast), reuse needs conveyance that the plant upgrade projects do not fund (SRC-TG-559, SRC-TG-652).

Salinity of effluent (industrial inputs, high-salt source water in the centre and south) is not removed by sand filtration and UV; reuse there needs salt-tolerant crops and drainage (SRC-TG-652, SRC-TG-654, SRC-TG-655).

blockers.blocker: Reuse for agriculture needs authorisation by the Minister of Agriculture, with the agreement of the Ministers of Environment and Public Health (Decree 89-1047 of 28 July 1989, amended by Decree 93-2447 of 13 December 1993). The AfDB finds the framework "incomplete and not based on a risk analysis" and the NT 106.03 standard (1989) takes a prescriptive approach, unlike the WHO health-risk approach.

Crop restriction. Irrigating vegetables and crops eaten raw with treated wastewater is prohibited, as is direct grazing on irrigated plots. This keeps reuse on orchards, fodder, cereals and industrial crops, which earn less than vegetables. FAO (2002) says the water is "not suitable for crops that are economically profitable".

Farmers can substitute shallow groundwater, which costs only pumping up to about 50 m, and the treated-water price (unchanged since 1997 at TND 0.02/m3) is already far below treatment cost (TND 0.3 to 0.7/m3), so a price cut cannot raise uptake and a price rise would compete with free-pumped groundwater.

Only 31 of 127 plants have tertiary treatment; 72.42% of treated water met the standards in 2024; the older plant stock (36% over 20 years old) produces effluent designed for discharge to rivers, not for users.

Weak operation of the framework. Authorisation is centralised, project ownership is split between agencies, and monitoring teams lack capacity (AfDB 1.2.6). Deputies note no strategic view of how treated water will be used (SRC-TG-559).
Farmer distrust of water quality and worries about marketing of crops, even where stated acceptance is high.

Sanitation charges cover only about 60 to 65% of ONAS operating costs (assessments of 2014/16), so ONAS depends on state subsidy; a 30% tariff rise was decided in October 2022 and further rises are forecast. Plant upgrades are financed by foreign loans (EUR 81.9 million for PAQEE-RCC, state-guaranteed).

criticisms.criticism: Treatment is designed for discharge, not for user needs, so reuse stagnates at 10% or less despite a stated 80% target.
Reuse projects are poorly planned, with no clear urban-planning plans or strategic view of how to use treated water, and sewer maintenance is poor.
criticisms.from: Deputies on the Finance Committee of the Assembly (2024)

criticisms.criticism: The reuse rules are not based on risk analysis, pathogen removal "has rarely been considered as a goal", and plants fail BOD5, COD and suspended-solids limits.
criticisms.from: AfDB appraisal team, citing the Water REUSE 2050 study

criticisms.criticism: Low reuse is not mainly about quality. Farmers have cheap alternatives (shallow groundwater), most effluent is far from farmland, and demand plateaued at 25 to 30% of treated water even after a price incentive.
criticisms.from: Drechsel and Hanjra case (citing Abu-Madi et al. 2008, GWI 2010, Qadir et al. 2010)

criticisms.criticism: Reuse programmes report potential area, not area irrigated. Equipped area exceeded actual area for years (actual about 47% of equipped in 2000-2009).

tradeOffs.effect: Salinity. Soil irrigated with treated wastewater was 127% more saline than groundwater-irrigated soil, particularly deeper down, though sodicity indexes were lower (abstract only, two perimeters).
Boron moved from topsoil to groundwater over three decades in Cebala Borj-Touil; boron in drainage water and groundwater slightly exceeded the standard in some periods.
Health risk to farmers and consumers is named in the AfDB environmental risk section; FAO (2002) reported insufficient medical care for agricultural workers. Neither source measures disease cases.

Energy. Tertiary treatment adds equipment, and energy is about 60% of ONAS operating cost. The AfDB project claims net power savings and solar offsets, but gives no kWh per m3 for tertiary treatment. Pumping to remote farms is not quantified in any source opened.

Benefits outside the target. Reuse reduces effluent discharge to rivers and the sea (Raoued sea samples compliant after the outfall, SRC-TG-556 via FND-TG-550), cuts fertiliser need through nutrients in the water, and in coastal aquifers could replace pumped groundwater.

gapLeft: Reuse adds a modest, bounded volume (about 290 to 300 Mm3 a year, possibly doubling by 2050 per AfDB). It does not touch the demand-side root causes in FND-TG-501 (subsidised tariffs, 80% of resources to irrigation, groundwater use above 100%). Actual uptake is not tracked on a consistent basis, so the benefit to the water balance is unknown. Salt and boron accumulation in reuse soils and groundwater has no monitoring owner and no phase 1 finding.
conflictOfInterest: none. The owner (ONAS) and the financiers (AfDB, AFD, JICA, World Bank) have no link to TahaGHZ or to expert EXP-TG-001 (STC) in the records read. The AfDB and World Bank appraise and describe projects they fund, so their benefit figures are treated as claims.
author: TahaGHZ

(3) Open the full texts of SRC-TG-654 and SRC-TG-655 (abstracts only seen). (4) Find the ex-post evaluation of PAQEE 1 and actual irrigated area at upgraded plants. excerpt: Tunisia treats about 293 million m3 of sewage a year in 127 ONAS plants and aims to turn it into irrigation water. The solution has four parts: - Tertiary upgrades at selected plants: sand filter, UV and similar. -…

sections.heading: What it is
sections.content:
Tunisia treats about 293 million m3 of sewage a year in 127 ONAS plants and aims to turn it into irrigation water (SRC-TG-530). The solution has four parts:
- Tertiary upgrades at selected plants: sand filter, UV and similar (SRC-TG-650).
- Irrigated perimeters supplied with treated water through the CRDA and GDA user groups (SRC-TG-652).
- Legal rules: Decree 89-1047 of 1989 as amended in 1993, standard NT 106.03, and a crop list (SRC-TG-650, SRC-TG-557).
- Strategy: Eau 2050 and "Water REUSE 2050", with a stated 80% use target for 2050 (SRC-TG-530).

Phase 1 of the AfDB-financed upgrade programme (PAQEE, 2012) rehabilitated about thirty plants. Phase 2 (PAQEE-RCC, 2024) funds 18 to 19 plants with a EUR 81.9 million loan (SRC-TG-650, SRC-TG-559). The Northern Tunis project in Borj Touil is a flagship case (SRC-TG-556).

sections.heading: What it claims, and what the evidence shows
sections.content:
**Volumes do not match the target.** Three official series disagree, which is itself a finding:
- 22 of 292 Mm3 reused in 2017, a direct rate of 8% (SRC-TG-650).
- 57 of 293 Mm3 per year at end-2023 (about 19%), stated orally by ONAS to a parliamentary committee (SRC-TG-559).
- 10 Mm3 (2023) and 11.3 Mm3 (2024) used for irrigation out of 293 and 295.7 Mm3 treated, about 3.4% and 3.8% (SRC-TG-530).

The ministry report itself says the use rate "stagne" at 10% at most (SRC-TG-530). The 57 Mm3 probably includes other uses, but this is not stated. Area actually irrigated was 2,425 ha (2021), 2,725 (2022), 2,577 (2023) and 2,778 ha (2024) (SRC-TG-530). Against that, PAQEE alone was said to give potential for 12,500 ha (SRC-TG-650).

**Potential versus actual is an old gap.** In 2000-2009 the area actually irrigated averaged 47% of equipped area (SRC-TG-651). Demand for treated water plateaued at 25 to 30% of treated volume even though it was priced 3 to 4 times below freshwater (SRC-TG-652). FAO's 2002 paper already said the water was available but "not suitable for crops that are economically profitable", is still echoed in the crop restrictions (SRC-TG-653, SRC-TG-557).

**Upgrades act on a real bottleneck.** The AfDB reports that stakeholders in the REUSE 2050 survey called quality "sometimes the main hindrance" (SRC-TG-650), and the ministry says treatment ignores user needs (SRC-TG-530). JICA reports 28 of 125 plants with tertiary treatment in 2021 (SRC-TG-558); the ministry reports 31 of 127 in 2024 (SRC-TG-530). That is a rise of three plants in three years. Outcomes of the 2012 phase (how many hectares were actually irrigated after upgrades) were not found.

sections.heading: Audit
sections.content:
**root_cause_coverage: 1.** FND-TG-550 names two root causes: effluent quality and conveyance. The programme acts on the first. It funds no transfer lines. For FND-TG-501, the root causes are climate decline, demand growth, and subsidised tariffs that encouraged over-use. Reuse adds supply and leaves all three in place. Supply of 290 to 300 Mm3 a year, if fully used, covers about a quarter of the 2050 deficit (SRC-TG-504 via FND-TG-501).

**evidence_quality: 1.** Evidence on effects is thin. The sources opened are lenders' appraisals (targets, not outcomes), a ministry sector report with inconsistent series, and oral statements recorded in a parliamentary report. No ex-post evaluation of PAQEE 1 was found. The soil studies are peer-reviewed but were seen as abstracts only.

**adoption: 1.** Widely deployed (127 plants, hundreds of hectares to a few thousand under irrigation), but actual use is 3 to 4% on the ministry's series, and the 80% target is far away.

**side_effects: 2.** Salinity and boron build-up are documented at perimeter scale but not as yield losses. Health risk is flagged by the lender but not measured. Offsetting benefits exist (less discharge, fertiliser savings). Energy effects are unquantified. Hence moderate, not none known.

**cost_accessibility: 1.** The price to farmers (TND 0.02/m3, unchanged since 1997) is a fraction of the TND 0.3 to 0.7/m3 treatment cost (SRC-TG-652), so the state and foreign lenders carry the cost. As an indicative figure only, EUR 81.9 million for about 3,357 ha is roughly EUR 24,000 per hectare, but the loan also pays for equipment renewal and solar PV, so this overstates the irrigation cost. ONAS's own financing depends on state aid and tariff rises.

sections.heading: Limits and blockers
sections.content: See the front matter for each blocker with its type. Legal text: Decree 89-1047 (1989), amended by Decree 93-2447 (1993), allows agricultural use only on authorisation by the Agriculture Minister after agreement of the Environment and Health Ministers, and only after treatment that meets current standards (SRC-TG-650). It also sets, via NT 106.03, a prohibition on irrigating vegetables and crops eaten raw and on direct grazing (SRC-TG-557, a consultant's second-hand report; the JORT text and the crop-list order were not opened). A revised Water Code was before Parliament at the time of the AfDB report and would allow use-specific standards based on risk analysis (SRC-TG-650); its adoption status was not checked.

sections.heading: Criticisms
sections.content: Listed in front matter. Two points stand out. First, the sources disagree on the cause of low uptake: the lenders and ministry stress quality, while the economic literature stresses cheap alternatives, distance and crop restrictions. The evidence we hold supports both, with quality plausible for some plants (72.42% compliance in 2024, SRC-TG-530) but no source opened shows how much of the 25 to 30% plateau quality explains, since plant-level compliance and use were not compared. Second, nothing opened shows that upgraded plants led to proportionally higher use.

sections.heading: Trade-offs and consequences
sections.content:
- **Agriculture (long-term, observed):** soil salinity and boron accumulation under long-term irrigation (SRC-TG-654, SRC-TG-655). Whether this lowers yields was not shown. No existing finding covers this. It should go to the agriculture lane owner for phase 1 as a candidate: "Salt and boron accumulation in soils and aquifers under treated-wastewater irrigation".
- **Water (observed locally):** boron reaching groundwater at Cebala Borj-Touil (SRC-TG-655).
- **Energy (not quantified):** energy is about 60% of ONAS operating cost (SRC-TG-652); tertiary treatment and pumping add load. The only offset figure is the AfDB's own projection (SRC-TG-650). Any energy figure here needs a kWh per m3 source.
- **Health (risk flagged, not measured):** AfDB names illness among farmers and consumers as a project risk (SRC-TG-650).
- **Public finance:** ONAS operates at a deficit covered by state balancing subsidies; new loans add guaranteed debt (SRC-TG-559, SRC-TG-650).
- **Projection, not observation:** the AfDB statement that treated water "will possibly more than double by 2050" is a projection (SRC-TG-650).

sections.heading: Verdict and gap
sections.content:
Partially solves. It acts on a real technical cause for part of the problem and delivers a modest, bounded supply, but does not address pricing, crop rules, distance or seasonality, and it cannot close the 2050 deficit. It works at small scale (the Ouardanine model, SRC-TG-652) and is not widely adopted, which is a delivery and design problem rather than a proof that reuse fails.

Phase 3 could examine: pairing upgrades with funded transfer lines and storage; reviewing crop lists and standards on a WHO-style risk basis; salinity management and drainage in reuse perimeters; reuse targeted at coastal aquifers where groundwater is over-pumped (SRC-TG-653); and consistent metering of reuse. Regional comparators (Jordan, Morocco, Egypt) were not audited in this record and are not claimed.

sections.heading: Verification
sections.content: **Outstanding verification:** (1) The SRC-TG-530 record lacks the extracts for Tables VI.5, VI.6, XI.8 and the REUT text (80% target, 10% stagnation, 31 tertiary plants, 72.42% compliance); the owner should add them. They were read from the original PDF on 2026-11-22. (2) Open the Water REUSE 2050 reports (AFD) for the diagnosis and the transfer-cost estimates. (3) Open the full texts of SRC-TG-654 and SRC-TG-655 (abstracts only seen). (4) Find the ex-post evaluation of PAQEE 1 and actual irrigated area at upgraded plants. (5) Find kWh per m3 for tertiary treatment and for conveyance in Tunisia. (6) Check the JORT texts of Decree 89-1047, Decree 93-2447 and the crop-list order, and the status of the new Water Code. (7) Open the original Abu-Madi et al. (2008) and GWI (2010) cited in SRC-TG-652. (8) Reconcile the 8%, 19% and 3.8% reuse series with ONAS and DGGREE. (9) Regional comparison (Jordan, Morocco, Egypt) was not done.

targetItems.title: Treated wastewater reuse remains limited and unevenly enabled
Without action, Tunisia's water balance is projected to turn negative by 2050 under RCP8.5, leaving about 28% of demand unmet; Eau 2050 flags a certain risk of a water crash from 2030 without figures

resolvedSources.title: Tunisie – Contribution aux éléments de la phase préparatoire du processus du Plan National d'Adaptation (Axe 2): Impacts des effets du changement climatique sur la sécurité alimentaire (Livrable 3/5, version finale)
resolvedSources.publisher: Agence Française de Développement (Facilité Adapt'Action) with MARHP; hosted by ONAGRI
resolvedSources.extracts:
Executive summary, printed page 10 (precipitation):

> une diminution des précipitations annuelles (entre -6% et -9% en 2050 et entre -9% et -18% en 2100 par rapport à la période de référence 1981-2010) sont attendues sous changement climatique

English gloss: Annual precipitation is expected to fall by 6-9% by 2050 and by 9-18% by 2100, relative to the 1981-2010 reference.

Executive summary, printed pages 10-11 (runoff, per capita):

> montrent une nette diminution des apports en eau qui varie selon les scénarios de 25 à 36% à l'horizon 2050 et de 33 à 61% à l'horizon 2100. En considérant uniquement l'élévation de température et en prenant une pluviométrie constante jusqu'à 2100, les écoulements baissent de 7 à 11% en 2050 et de 9 à 20% en 2100 selon les différentes formules. Nous constatons que le tiers de la diminution des écoulements est dû à l'augmentation de l'évapotranspiration et les 2/3 reviennent à la diminution de la quantité de pluie.

> Le quota en ressources renouvelables par habitant et par an pourrait passer de 366 m3 actuellement à 200 m3 en 2050 et moins de 150 m3 en 2100.

English gloss: Inflows fall by 25-36% by 2050 and by 33-61% by 2100, depending on scenario. With rainfall held constant (warming only), runoff falls by 7-11% by 2050. One third of the decline comes from higher evapotranspiration and two thirds from less rain. Renewable resources per inhabitant would go from 366 m3/yr now to 200 m3 in 2050 and below 150 m3 in 2100.

Section 2.2, printed page 40 (historical baseline):

> Durant les 3 dernières décennies (90/91-2015/2016), on a enregistré 11 années hydrologiquement sèches pour uniquement 6 années humides. L'apport moyen en eau de surface pour la période est de l'ordre de 2700 millions de m3.

English gloss: Over 1990/91-2015/16 there were 11 hydrologically dry years against 6 wet ones. Mean surface inflow for the period was about 2,700 Mm3.

Table 6, printed page 42, as extracted with `pdftotext -raw`. Columns: reference period, RCP4.5 2050, RCP4.5 2100, RCP8.5 2050, RCP8.5 2100, official MARHP value.

> National Apports 2494 1645 1577 1762 1025 2700
> Variation en % -34% -37% -29% -59%

English gloss: National surface inflow is 2,494 Mm3 in the modelled reference period. It falls to 1,645 (-34%) under RCP4.5 by 2050 and to 1,762 (-29%) under RCP8.5 by 2050. By 2100 it falls to 1,577 (RCP4.5) and 1,025 (RCP8.5). The official MARHP value is 2,700 Mm3.

Printed page 42, below Table 6:

> Une étude récente13 montre que les évènements extrêmes de précipitations pourraient être moins fréquents et moins intenses au Sud de la Méditerranée qu'au Nord sous l'effet du changement climatique. L'idée selon laquelle, des précipitations extrêmes plus fréquentes et plus copieuses pourraient être suffisantes en 2050 pour recharger les ouvrages et les nappes apparaît donc comme une hypothèse particulièrement optimiste.

English gloss: Extreme rainfall may become less frequent and less intense south of the Mediterranean. The idea that bigger storms will refill dams and aquifers by 2050 is therefore "particularly optimistic".

Printed page 42 (agriculture's share of resources):

> Une nouvelle approche de l'allocation des ressources devient inéluctable et aura un impact très important sur les différents secteurs et surtout le secteur agricole qui exploite plus de 80% des ressources.

English gloss: A new approach to allocating water becomes unavoidable and will hit agriculture hardest, since it uses more than 80% of resources.

Printed page 43 (groundwater, coastal aquifers):

> Les eaux souterraines renouvelables pourraient passer de 1524 millions de m3 actuellement à pratiquement 1000 millions de m3 en 2050 et 700 millions en 2100, soit la moitié des ressources actuelles. Au niveau des nappes côtières les pertes seront plus importantes à la suite de l'élévation du niveau de la mer et pourraient atteindre 50% de leurs ressources en 2050 et beaucoup plus en 2100.

English gloss: Renewable groundwater would go from 1,524 Mm3 now to about 1,000 Mm3 in 2050 and 700 Mm3 in 2100. Losses in coastal aquifers will be larger because of sea-level rise and could reach 50% of their resources by 2050.

Table 8, printed page 43 (`-raw`). Columns: official MARHP value (Mm3), RCP4.5 2050, RCP4.5 2100, RCP8.5 2050, RCP8.5 2100.

> Total 1620 1069 1021 1150 664
> Variation en % -34% -37% -29% -59%

English gloss: Groundwater resources go from 1,620 Mm3 (official) to 1,069 (RCP4.5) or 1,150 (RCP8.5) Mm3 by 2050.

Section 2.2.4, printed page 44:

> Les nappes côtières qui connaissent une surexploitation subiront une accélération de l'intrusion marine sous l'effet de la remonté du niveau de la mer estimée entre 30 et 50 cm en 2050. Environ la moitié des réserves dans les nappes phréatiques littorales risquent de disparaitre.

English gloss: Overexploited coastal aquifers will see accelerated seawater intrusion as the sea rises by an estimated 30-50 cm by 2050. About half of the reserves in coastal shallow aquifers risk disappearing.

Executive summary, printed page 17 (demand):

> La demande totale en eau augmenterait autour de 38%. Cependant, les ressources risquent de baisser considérablement avec moins 28% en 2050 et moins 59% en 2100, creusant fortement le déficit hydrique.

English gloss: Total water demand would rise by about 38%, while resources may fall by 28% by 2050 and 59% by 2100.

Section 3.3.2, printed page 115:

> La demande en eau bleue a été estimée à 3,1 milliards de m3 en 2018. Elle est satisfaite par une exploitation intensive des eaux souterraines s'élevant à plus de 123% des ressources totales.

> Au cours de la troisième année de sècheresse 2015/2018, le quota alloué aux périmètres publics irrigués a été réduit à 27% par rapport à l'approvisionnement habituel27.

> En 2018, trois quarts des ressources exploitées sont consommées par le secteur agricole pour l'irrigation de 406 540 ha, soit un volume de 2,4 milliards de m3, dont 84% provient des eaux souterraines et seulement 16% des eaux des barrages.

English gloss: Blue-water demand was 3.1 billion m3 in 2018, met by groundwater exploitation above 123% of total resources. In the third drought year of 2015-2018, quotas for public irrigated schemes were cut to 27% of normal supply. In 2018, agriculture used three quarters of exploited resources, 2.4 billion m3 for 406,540 ha, 84% of it from groundwater.

Printed pages 115-116 (assumptions behind the balances; the 913 Mm3 sentence starts on page 115, the other sentences are on page 116):

> qui atteindrait 913 millions de M3 en 2050

> des ressources non conventionnelles mobilisables incluant REUT et dessalement, soit 626 millions de M3, ce qui représente dix les volumes actuels réutilisés et dessalés
> des économies d'eau de l'ordre de 900 millions de M3

> Les hypothèses ainsi retenues, permettent de montrer un bilan potentiellement excédentaire de 16% en 2050 sous réserve que soient assurés les investissements pour mobiliser les ressources non conventionnelles, éviter les pertes d'eau dans les réseaux et améliorer la collecte des eaux pluviales.

> les données STUDI-GKW ont été corrigées pour prendre en compte la hausse de l'évapotranspiration, qui augmente ,la demande de l'ordre de 4.6 % en 2050 et 9.1% en 2100

> l'importation nette d'eau virtuelle ­ estimée en 2013 à 4,7 milliards de m330, est en train de dépasser sensiblement le volume des ressources nationales.

English gloss: Drinking-water demand reaches 913 Mm3 in 2050 (STUDI-GKW). The Eau 2050 scenario adds 626 Mm3 of reuse and desalination (ten times current volumes) and about 900 Mm3 of savings. That gives a potential 16% surplus in 2050, provided the investments are made. Higher evapotranspiration raises irrigation demand by 4.6% (2050) and 9.1% (2100). Net virtual-water imports (4.7 billion m3 in 2013) are overtaking national resources.

Table 30, printed page 115 (`pdftotext -raw`). Columns: 2018 MARHP | ITES 2050 | STUDI (Eau 2050) 2050 | PNA RCP8.5 2050 | PNA RCP8.5 2100.

> Eau agricole 2440 2000* 3063 3204 3342
> Eau potable 663 1300** 913 913 913
> Demande totale 3103 3300 3976 4117 4255
> Eaux conventionelles 4508 4508 3101 2912 1689
> Non conventionnelles 66 626 66 66
> Economies d'eau 867
> Ressourcestotales 4574 4508 4594 2978 1755
> 1471 1208 618 -1139 -2500
> 147% 137% 116% 72% 41%
> Bilan Demande/ ressourcesmm3
> Taux de couverture de lademande

English gloss: Total demand is 3,103 Mm3 (2018), 3,976 Mm3 (STUDI 2050), 4,117 Mm3 (PNA RCP8.5 2050) and 4,255 Mm3 (2100). Conventional resources go from 4,508 Mm3 (2018) to 3,101 (STUDI 2050), 2,912 (PNA RCP8.5 2050) and 1,689 Mm3 (2100). Total resources are 4,574, 4,594 (STUDI, including 626 non-conventional and 867 savings), 2,978 and 1,755 Mm3. The balance is +1,471, +1,208, +618, -1,139 and -2,500 Mm3. Coverage of demand is 147%, 137%, 116%, 72% and 41%.

Printed page 115, below Table 30 (the ITES column):

> Les prévisions déjà publiées à l'horizon 2050 (ITES) se basent sur l'hypothèse d'une baisse maitrisée de la demande en eau agricole et sur une augmentation sensible de la demande en eau potable tous secteurs confondus (domestique, industriel, touristique) selon le MARHP dans la stratégie EAU2030, mais ne tient pas compte les effets du CC sur les ressources comme sur la demande.

English gloss: The earlier published 2050 projections (ITES) assume a controlled fall in agricultural water demand and a marked rise in drinking-water demand (MARHP Eau 2030 strategy), but do not account for climate change effects on resources or demand.

Printed page 116 (reuse of STUDI-GKW inputs):

> Les hypothèses retenues dans la présente étude tiennent compte des calculs de STUDI-GKW sur les ressources et la demande en eau agricole et eau potable.

English gloss: This study's assumptions take into account STUDI-GKW's calculations of resources and of agricultural and drinking-water demand.

Printed page 116, text after Table 30:

> Les ressources conventionnelles mobilisables (eaux bleues) pourraient diminuer de 35% en 2050 et de 63% en 2100 par rapport aux observations de 2018. L'estimation pour l'horizon 2050 est très proche (- 6%) de celle proposée par STUDI-GKW.

> La demande totale en 2050 ressort à 4,1 milliards de m3, soit 4% de plus que dans l'estimation du rapport Eau 2050.

> Sous l'effet des changements climatiques, le bilan hydrique des eaux bleues deviendrait donc négatif pour la première fois avec une couverture des besoins par les ressources de 72% en 2050 et 41% en 2100.

English gloss: Mobilisable conventional blue water could fall by 35% by 2050 and 63% by 2100 versus 2018, within 6% of the Eau 2050 (STUDI-GKW) estimate. Total 2050 demand is 4.1 billion m3, 4% above Eau 2050. The blue-water balance would turn negative for the first time, with 72% coverage in 2050 and 41% in 2100.

- Opened via: curl+pdftotext (layout, plus `-raw` for pages 42, 43 and 115); saw: full text, about 120 pages.
- Dated April 2021 ("Avril 2021 – Version finale"). The World Bank CCDR cites it as "Agence française de développement, 2020"; the tables say "Élaboration étude, 2020".
- Method: national 5 km climate model, 1981-2100, under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5. Runoff comes from empirical water-balance formulas (Tixeront, Turc, Schreiber), not a calibrated hydrological model. Groundwater recharge is assumed to change by the same rate as surface runoff, which is a strong simplification.
- Internal inconsistencies:
  - Renewable groundwater is 1,524 Mm3 in the text but 1,620 Mm3 in Table 8.
  - The 2100 range for the runoff decline is 33-61% in the summary but 31-61% in the body.
  - The modelled reference runoff (2,494 Mm3) is below the official MARHP 2,700 Mm3.
  - Page 40 gives blue-water potential of about 4.8 billion m3, or 436 m3 per inhabitant per year, while pages 11 and 43 give 366 m3 of renewable resources per inhabitant. The two figures use different numerators.
- Independence: the 2050 balances reuse STUDI-GKW (Eau 2050) resource and demand calculations (page 116), and the 2018 column is MARHP data. Agreement with SRC-TG-503 is therefore not independent confirmation.
- Verified by the source-verifier on 2026-11-21: the ONAGRI file was re-downloaded, and all extracts match the document at the pages given.
- Table 30 values come from the `-raw` extraction. Row labels for the last two rows are printed after the numbers. The column mapping was checked by arithmetic: 4574-3103 = 1471, 2978-4117 = -1139, 2978/4117 = 72%, 4594-3976 = 618.
- In the ITES column, the asterisked values (2000*, 1300**) mark different source studies, per the table footnote: "* ITES -Eau 2050 **MARHP stratégie Eau 2030 *** Rapport Eau 2050 Étape 3 vol2, STUDI."

resolvedSources.title: Rapport national du secteur de l'eau, année 2024
resolvedSources.publisher: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Ressources Hydrauliques et de la Pêche (MARHP), Bureau de la Planification et des Equilibres Hydrauliques; hosted by ONAGRI
resolvedSources.extracts:
Synthèse générale, printed page 7:

> Au niveau de la demande, les quotas de l'irrigation ont été fortement réduits pour assurer la pérennité de l'arboriculture. Le volume consommé à partir des barrages est passé de 88,4 Mm3 en 2022-2023 à 46,7 Mm3 en 2023-2024.

> En bref, les mesures prises face au manque d'eau ont pu assurer l'approvisionnement en eau potable, mais l'agriculture irriguée a été clairement affectée.

> Les périmètres irrigués à partir des barrages n'ont pu bénéficier que de quantités minimes insuffisantes même au maintien de l'arboriculture. Les PPI irrigués à partir de Sidi Salem n'ont pu bénéficier que de 12 Mm3 pour des besoins dépassant les 100 millions.

> Les PPI de Nebhana spécialisés dans les cultures primeurs maraichères sous serre n'ont pu bénéficier d'eau d'irrigation et se sont trouvés en arrêt total avec toutes les conséquences négatives qui en résultent : baisse de la production nationale et montée des prix, pas de revenus des agriculteurs, terres délaissées et vouées aux extensions de l'urbanisme, GDA en chômage, ...

> Par ailleurs, le secteur irrigué s'est basé sur les ressources souterraines ce qui contribue à la croissance de leur surexploitation et la dégradation de leur qualité.

> Ce secteur rencontre des limites en termes d'intensification avec un taux global moyen de l'ordre de 90% mais très variable d'un périmètre à un autre en fonction de la situation du contexte socioéconomique.

English gloss (last sentence): The sector faces limits on intensification, with an overall average rate of about 90% but very variable from one perimeter to another.

English gloss: Irrigation quotas were cut sharply to keep orchards alive; consumption from dams fell from 88.4 Mm3 (2022-23) to 46.7 Mm3 (2023-24). Drinking water was secured but irrigated agriculture was "clearly affected". Dam-fed perimeters got minimal volumes, insufficient even for orchards; Sidi Salem PPIs got 12 Mm3 against needs above 100 Mm3. Nebhana PPIs, specialised in greenhouse early vegetables, got no irrigation water and stopped entirely: lower national output and higher prices, no farmer income, land abandoned to urban sprawl, GDAs idle. The irrigated sector fell back on groundwater, worsening overexploitation and quality.

Section II.1 "Restrictions d'usages" (irrigation), printed page 39:

> Le MARHP a notifié aux CRDAs de ne pas programmer les cultures d'été et les cultures consommatrices d'eau telles que les cucurbitacées et les légumes, et de limiter aux arbres fruitiers et aux cultures stratégiques (fourrages, betteraves sucrières et grandes cultures) dans les limites des quotas qui seront alloués aux périmètres irrigués liés aux barrages. Le volume consommé total à partir des barrages est passé de 88,4 Mm3 en 2022-2023 à 46,7 Mm3 en 2023-2024 (source : DGGREE),

> Le volume exploité à partir du système Mellègue-Bouhertma a été de l'ordre de 22 Mm3 contre 51 Mm3 l'année précédente (source : DGGREE),

> Malgré la faiblesse du quota alloué aux CRDA à partir du barrage Sidi Salem en 2023-2024 qui était de 22 Mm3, les CRDA n'ont pu bénéficier que de 12 Mm3. Le pompage illicite de l'eau lâchée à la Medjerda à partir de Sidi Salem pour atteindre les périmètres irrigués est parmi les causes essentielles de l'indisponibilité réelle du quota,

> La SECADENORD a facturé un volume total de 13 Mm3 aux CRDA en 2024 contre 23 en 2023 et 50 en 2022 (source : SECADENORD).

English gloss: The ministry told CRDAs not to plan summer crops or water-hungry crops (cucurbits, vegetables) and to limit irrigation from dams to fruit trees and "strategic" crops (fodder, sugar beet, field crops) within quotas. Total consumption from dams: 88.4 Mm3 (2022-23) to 46.7 Mm3 (2023-24). Mellègue-Bouhertma: 22 Mm3 against 51 Mm3 the year before. Sidi Salem quota for 2023-24 was 22 Mm3 but CRDAs received only 12 Mm3, mainly because of illicit pumping of the water released into the Medjerda. SECADENORD billed CRDAs 13 Mm3 in 2024, 23 in 2023, 50 in 2022.

Printed page 43:

> En irrigation, le système de quotas est encore plus sévère en 2024. Les volumes exploités à partir des barrages sont pratiquement réduits à moitié par rapport à 2023.

English gloss: In 2024 the irrigation quota system was even more severe; volumes used from dams were nearly halved compared with 2023.

Section I.4 "L'économie de l'eau d'irrigation", printed pages 58-59:

> Le Programme National d'Economie de l'EAU en Irrigation PNEEI a permis d'équiper 428 500 ha en équipements d'économie d'eau à la parcelle sur 442 500 ha de PI.

> L'irrigation localisée est pratiquée sur 219 900 ha, l'aspersion est pratiquée sur 113 900 ha. Le gravitaire amélioré est appliqué pour l'irrigation de 94 700 ha. Les investissements pour l'équipement en économie d'eau ont atteint depuis le démarrage du PNEE en 1995 jusqu'à 2024 le montant de 1709 MDT y compris les subventions.

English gloss: PNEEI has equipped 428,500 of 442,500 ha of irrigated perimeters (96.9%): drip 219,900 ha, sprinkler 113,900 ha, improved gravity 94,700 ha. Investment 1995-2024: 1,709 MTND including subsidies.

Conclusions, printed page 81:

> Quant à l'agriculture irriguée, les conditions hydriques défavorables ont causé certaines régressions sur la production des fruits et cultures maraichères. Les PPI de Nebhana n'ont pu bénéficier d'eau d'irrigation alors que les quotas alloués à ceux de la Basse Vallée de la Medjerda ont été très faibles.

English gloss: Unfavourable water conditions reduced fruit and vegetable production; Nebhana PPIs received no irrigation water and lower Medjerda PPIs very low quotas.
resolvedSources.notes:
- Opened via: curl + pdftotext (layout); saw: full text (184 pages). Latin-1 encoded; converted with iconv.
- Data year 2024 (irrigation campaign 2023-24); publication year 2025 inferred from press coverage of the "rapport 2024" in October 2025 (not opened as a source).
- The report gives no production figures by crop for 2023-24 in the passages read; effects are described qualitatively.
- 88.4 Mm3 (2022-23 consumption from all dams) and the 2023 report's Table 8 (Sidi Salem 18.7, Nebhana 4, Siliana group 4.8) are consistent in scale, but the 2023 report does not give an all-dam total.

resolvedSources.extracts:
Section 1.3.4.2 "Performances financières de l'ONAS", printed page 1-33 (PDF page 129):

Entre 2005 et 2009, le total des revenus a augmenté en moyenne de 3% par an, alors que le total des dépenses progressait de 7,5% par an. [...] Le déficit augmente donc en moyenne de 18% par année.

Summary chapter, "Durabilité financière" (PDF page 95):

> Bien que le coût du service ait augmenté annuellement, les prix ont été gelés depuis 2003 et cela a causé un plus grand déficit.

English gloss: Service costs rose every year but prices were frozen from 2003, widening the deficit. ONAS now depends heavily on State aid not only for investment and rehabilitation but also for day-to-day operation and maintenance.

Tariff-adjustment section (PDF page 114), ONAS projection without tariff adjustment (extracted with `pdftotext -raw`; columns 2010 to 2016):

> Taux de recouvrement des dépenses par la redevance d'assainissement (%) 56,3 49,5 52,9 52,2 51,0 49,3 47,8

> La concentration maximale de 0,1 et 0,05 mg/L de phosphore total exige également un effort important pour éliminer le phosphore des effluents, ce qui n'est possible que par voie physico-chimique.

> Ces documents légaux se trouvent actuellement en révision. Le projet de nouveau décret a été mis à disposition par l'ONAS.

> La réutilisation des eaux usées traitées en agriculture est réglementée par le Décret nº 89-1047 du 28 Juillet 1989, et par la norme tunisienne NT 106.03 (1989), qui définit les caractéristiques physico-chimiques et biologiques des eaux à réutiliser.

> L'utilisation des eaux usées traitées pour l'irrigation des cultures maraîchères et des crudités est interdite. Le pâturage direct dans les parcelles irriguées par les eaux usées traitées est également interdit.

English gloss: The NT 106.02 discharge limits of 0.1 and 0.05 mg/l total phosphorus can only be met with physico-chemical treatment. The discharge texts were under revision in 2012 (draft decree supplied by ONAS). Agricultural reuse is governed by Decree 89-1047 of 28 July 1989 and standard NT 106.03 (1989). Irrigating vegetable crops and crops eaten raw with treated wastewater is prohibited, as is direct grazing on plots irrigated with it.

resolvedSources.title: Rapport de l'étude préparatoire pour le projet de construction d'une station avancée de traitement des eaux usées à Gabès en République tunisienne
resolvedSources.publisher: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) for ONAS
resolvedSources.extracts:
Chapter 1, project background (PDF page 30):

> Dans ce contexte, le gouvernement tunisien a fixé l'objectif de réutiliser 50% ou plus des eaux usées épurées dans son Plan quinquennal de développement national (2016-2020) et a identifié la promotion de l'utilisation des eaux usées épurées comme une priorité dans le Plan de développement du secteur de l'assainissement « Réutilisation des eaux usées 2050 » en cours d'élaboration.

> Actuellement, 125 stations d'épuration sont en place dans les circonscriptions administratives et les régions de plus de 3 000 habitants relevant de l'Office National de l'Assainissement tunisien (ci-dessous repris « ONAS »). Cependant, seules 28 de ces stations sont équipées d'installations de traitement tertiaire telles que filtration et traitement par ultraviolets, et la qualité des eaux épurées dans les installations de traitement dépourvues d'équipements tertiaires n'est pas élevée, ce qui fait que seulement environ 21% du total des eaux usées épurées sont recyclées à des fins de protection de l'environnement, d'agriculture et d'irrigation, et la majorité rejetée dans les rivières et autres plans d'eau. (ONAS, 2021).

English gloss: The 2016-2020 five-year plan set a target of reusing 50% or more of treated wastewater. ONAS runs 125 plants; only 28 have tertiary treatment (filtration, UV). Effluent from plants without tertiary treatment is of low quality, so only about 21% of treated wastewater is recycled (environmental protection, agriculture, irrigation); most is discharged to rivers and other water bodies (ONAS, 2021).

resolvedSources.title: Water Reuse in the Arab World: From Principle to Practice - Voices from the Field (summary of expert consultation, Dubai, 22-24 May 2011)
resolvedSources.publisher: World Bank (with partners of the Expert Consultation on Wastewater Management in the Arab World)
resolvedSources.extracts:
Case Study 2, "Tunisia: Water reuse for Agriculture" (printed page 21):

> In Tunisia, the total area equipped for irrigation with treated wastewater has increased steadily, while the actual area irrigated with wastewater has varied significantly from year to year (Figure 1). The disconnect in trends can largely be explained by the variability in rainfall over the years with increases and decreases in areas corresponding with increases and decreases in surface water availability.

> From 2000-2009, the area effectively irrigated with treated wastewater represents on average 47% of the total area equipped for irrigation-a relatively low figure.

> Among 8065 ha that may be irrigated with reclaimed wastewater, 4646 ha (representing 59% of the total area) are equipped with saving water techniques. The rest is irrigated following the traditional practice of furrows and flooding.

> Significantly, efforts are underway for the transfer of treated wastewater from Tunis to the country's arid interior-with a long-term goal of irrigating over 25,000 ha and recharging aquifers with 30 million m3.

resolvedSources.title: Case: Wastewater and biosolids for fruit trees (Tunisia) - supporting case for Business Model 17 (book chapter 14, Pathways to cost recovery)
resolvedSources.publisher: Drechsel P. and Hanjra M.A.; Taylor & Francis (book on wastewater as a resource); open copy hosted on CGSpace
resolvedSources.extracts:
Market environment (printed page 571):

> Perception studies show a reasonably high level of farmers' hypothetical acceptance to use reclaimed wastewater (80%), preferably without restrictions, and public acceptance (71%) to consume crops irrigated with treated wastewater (Abu-Madi et al., 2008). However, despite increasing water shortages and substantial economic incentives, actual demand for reclaimed water between 2001 and 2009 plateaued at around 25-30% of treated wastewater. According to Abu-Madi et al. (2008) and GWI (2010), factors that fuel the farmers' hesitation are: (i) availability of or accessibility to freshwater; (ii) distrusted water quality; and (iii) worries about crop/fruit marketing and acceptance. Less important are however concern for public criticism, concern for health impacts, religious prohibition, or psychological aversion.

> Industrial pollution due to poor upstream pre-treatment (a legal requirement for industrials but often poorly observed in practice) which refers in particular to salinity in central and southern Tunisia.

Macro-economic environment (printed page 572):

> Sanitation charges for domestic users, industry and tourist establishments vary according to water consumption and the principle of `polluter pays' and do so far only cover about 60-65% of ONAS's operational costs, which comprise personnel salaries (about 30%), energy (60%) and equipment repairs and replacements (10%). The rest is financed by the state.

> The tariff set by the Government in 1997 demanded Tunisian dinar (TND) 0.02/m3 (ca. USD 0.02/m3 at that time, or USD 0.015/m3 in 2010). The target is to keep the price for reclaimed water significantly below the one of the subsidized freshwater which was about 3 to 4 times higher for irrigation [...] The price for reclaimed water has remained unchanged since 1997 and covers only a fraction of the real cost of wastewater treatment, estimated at TND0.3-0.7/m3 (GWI, 2010).

> Despite the low price charged to Tunisian farmers for reclaimed water compared to conventional water supply, the demand for reclaimed water remained so far modest (Qadir et al., 2010). The mismatch has (i) in part geographical reasons with most wastewater being produced in the Greater Tunis area and along the coast, i.e. not where it is mostly needed; (ii) is supported by the availability of alternative water sources like shallow groundwater which only attracts pumping costs until a depth of 50m (FAO, 2009); and (iii) is also driven by seasonal demand-supply gaps.

Executive summary:

> Nearly all (95%) of this water is treated at secondary level.
